items.followUp: A 2 kg object moving at 8 m s⁻¹ is brought to rest in 4 s. Find the force acting on it.

rubric.why: The mass, initial velocity, stopping time and final velocity are the given quantities needed for the calculation.
rubric.description: Identifies the given data in S.I. units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the given values.

rubric.why: Acceleration is found from the change in velocity divided by time.
rubric.description: States the acceleration formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: The change from 10 m s⁻¹ to zero in 2 s gives an acceleration of −5 m s⁻².
rubric.description: Calculates the acceleration correctly, including its sign.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct acceleration.

rubric.why: Newton’s second law relates force to mass and acceleration.
rubric.description: Uses Newton’s second law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct force relation.

rubric.why: The force has magnitude 25 N and acts opposite to the motion.
rubric.description: Gives the stopping force with its direction or signed value.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct force and direction.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 5 kg, u = 10 m s⁻¹, v = 0 m s⁻¹, t = 2 s.
Formula: a = (v − u) / t.
Substitution: a = (0 − 10) / 2 = −5 m s⁻².
Formula: F = ma.
Substitution: F = 5 × (−5) = −25 N.
The required force has magnitude 25 N and acts opposite to the motion.

items.followUp: Derive the formula for the kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with speed v.

rubric.why: Kinetic energy is the energy associated with the motion of a body.
rubric.description: Defines kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that kinetic energy is energy possessed due to motion.

rubric.why: The derivation uses the work relation and Newton’s second law.
rubric.description: Relates work done and force to displacement and acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both relations.

rubric.why: For a body starting from rest, the equation of motion gives its displacement in terms of its final speed.
rubric.description: Uses the equation of motion to obtain displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the equation of motion and the starting-from-rest condition.

rubric.why: Substituting the displacement into the work expression gives the kinetic-energy formula.
rubric.description: Obtains the formula for kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the derived result.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
Work done, W = Fs, and F = ma.
For a body starting from rest, u = 0 and v² − u² = 2as, so s = v² / 2a.
Therefore, KE = W = Fs = (ma)(v² / 2a) = ½mv².

items.followUp: A 20 cm spanner is used to apply a perpendicular force of 150 N to a nut. Find the torque.

rubric.why: The force is given in newtons and the spanner length must be converted to metres.
rubric.description: Identifies the force and converts the spanner length to S.I. units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the given force and the correct length conversion.

rubric.why: Torque is the product of force and perpendicular distance from the pivot.
rubric.description: States the torque relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: The converted distance and force are substituted into the torque formula.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution.

rubric.why: The product of 200 and 0.15 is 30.
rubric.description: Calculates the torque magnitude correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the numerical value 30.

rubric.why: Torque is expressed in newton metres.
rubric.description: Gives the S.I. unit of torque.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 200 N, d = 15 cm = 0.15 m.
Formula: torque, τ = Fd, where d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot.
Substitution: τ = 200 N × 0.15 m.
Answer: τ = 30 N m.

items.followUp: A wooden block has dimensions 30 cm × 10 cm × 4 cm and a mass of 600 g. Find its density in S.I. units.

rubric.why: Mass and dimensions are converted to S.I. units before calculating density.
rubric.description: Converts the mass and all three dimensions to S.I. units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversions.

rubric.why: The volume is the product of the block’s three dimensions.
rubric.description: Calculates the block’s volume correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct volume.

rubric.why: Density is mass divided by volume.
rubric.description: States the density formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Dividing the mass by the volume gives 425.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values and calculates the density magnitude.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution or numerical result.

rubric.why: The S.I. unit of density is kilograms per cubic metre.
rubric.description: Gives the density in S.I. units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct unit.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 850 g = 0.850 kg.
Dimensions: 40 cm = 0.40 m, 10 cm = 0.10 m, 5 cm = 0.05 m.
Formula: density, ρ = m / V.
Substitution: ρ = 0.850 kg / 0.002 m³ = 425 kg m⁻³.
Answer: the density of the wood is 425 kg m⁻³.

items.followUp: What is the least count of a vernier caliper?

rubric.why: Least count describes the smallest length an instrument can measure accurately.
rubric.description: Defines the least count of a screw gauge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: For a screw gauge, least count is calculated by dividing the pitch by the number of divisions on its circular scale.
rubric.description: Gives the screw-gauge least-count relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: The least count of a screw gauge is the smallest length it can measure accurately.
Least count = pitch of the screw / number of divisions on the circular scale.
